newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply down, nearbys limit.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply down, nearbys limit.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply lower in all months on Friday, as active technical selling from local investors emerged from the opening, traders said.
Nearby two months closed the daily 500 yen limit down, and the benchmark September 1997 contract was down 340 yen at 17,360 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 99,092 lots.

Active selling from local investors continued to push down the market, the traders said. "Investors holding long positions at nearby months actively liquidated them," a brokerage house trader said. Price gains of the CBOT corn were not enough to encourage investors to buy, they said.
Open interest as of September 5 was 510,207 lots.
The December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.34 per bushel at 0825 GMT, against $3.34-3/4 at Thursday's close.
The December CBOT soybean futures contract on the overnight trading system was at $7.94-3/4 per bushel at 0825 GMT, from $7.95-3/4 at Thursday's close.
